title: Human Approval and Recovery Boundaries
summary: A preview specification demonstrating how to teach approval gates and ambiguous side effects safely. This is not a published or fact-checked lesson.
objectives: Describe why an approval gate must be enforced by trusted controller code.
Distinguish a confirmed failure from an ambiguous side-effect outcome.

sections.title: Approval gate as state transition
paragraphs: A model can recommend a high-impact action but should not approve its own action. Trusted controller code checks authenticated permissions and a recorded approval before any write.
A user-facing review step should display the exact action, destination, and data to be sent. An approval must be scoped to this particular operation, not silently reused for another request.

sections.title: Ambiguous outcomes
paragraphs: If a remote write times out, the request may have succeeded even though the caller received no acknowledgement. The controller records UNKNOWN and attempts read-only reconciliation before considering a retry.
Without a provider idempotency guarantee or reliable reconciliation, escalate the outcome for manual handling rather than automatically replaying a potentially duplicated side effect.

sections.title: Explore a retry budget
paragraphs: Changing the allowed number of attempts affects the illustrative request budget. This exercise makes the arithmetic visible without making any network calls.

interactive.explanation: Two extra retries plus the original attempt equals three attempts.

quiz.prompt: Who enforces approval for a high-impact agent action?
quiz.explanation: Approval is a security boundary, so authorization belongs in code outside model output.

quiz.prompt: What does UNKNOWN mean after a timed-out external write?
options: The outcome could be success or failure
quiz.explanation: A lost acknowledgment leaves a possibly completed side effect; reconciliation is required.

quiz.prompt: What is the safest default without replay guarantees?
options: Change the operation identifier and resend
quiz.explanation: An ambiguous side effect cannot be safely repeated absent provider guarantees or reconciliation.

interview: Design an approval workflow that withstands stale workers, model prompt injection and changing user permissions.
Explain an audit trail and recovery strategy for a request that times out after an external payment or email API call.

lab.title: Approval gate simulator
instructions: Implement an operation record with status DRAFT, AWAITING_APPROVAL, APPROVED and EXECUTED.
Reject execution until an authenticated approval with matching operation ID and payload digest exists.
Write deterministic tests for expired approvals, mismatched hashes and ambiguous tool timeouts.
lab.expected: An unauthorized or ambiguous action never silently executes or replays.
